children: Shares of computer processor maker AMD

jumped 8% in the morning session after the company announced in an official press release that its fifth-generation AMD EPYC server CPUs are powering the host foundation for Google Cloud TPU 8tx, establishing hardware-enforced confidential computing for cloud artificial intelligence systems.

The expanded deployment with Google Cloud underscores sustained enterprise demand for AMD's high-performance data center processors. Separately, Oppenheimer upgraded the stock to a Buy rating, TipRanks reported.

The bullish rating from Oppenheimer highlights growing confidence in the chipmaker's competitive positioning. Contributing to the momentum, the major indices rebounded with the tech heavy Nasdaq index up more than 2% in the morning session as dip buyers stepped in following a severe rout driven by artificial intelligence names in the previous week.
What is the market telling us

AMD’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 56 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock gained 11.3% on the news that dip-buyers moved into beaten-down semiconductor and hardware names following the sector's steepest one-day rout in 19 months.

The turnaround gained traction after President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that he is 100% in favor of artificial intelligence infrastructure, calling data centers "GOLD" and pledging to help states expand capacity, in comments carried by CNBC. That endorsement eased worries ignited by Democratic midterm victories and calls for data-center project halts.

AMD is up 122% since the beginning of the year, but at $496.19 per share, it is still trading 23.6% below its 52-week high of $649.42 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of AMD’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $3,332.
